text: Before you respond to the next person who complains to you today, pause and silently name one concrete reason their frustration makes sense from where they're standing, then respond.
Today, tell one person something true you've been softening or avoiding, in a single direct sentence, without padding it with qualifiers.
The next time you feel rushed or irritated waiting on someone today, take three slow breaths before you speak or act, and notice if your response changes.
Identify one person today who seems overlooked or left out of a conversation, and deliberately ask them a specific question about themselves.
Pick one belief you hold strongly and write down the single strongest argument against it that you can construct honestly, not a strawman.
In your next conversation where you're confident you're right, ask one genuine question that could reveal you're missing something, before stating your view.
When something goes wrong today, out loud or in writing, name it as 'a setback I can respond to' instead of 'a disaster,' and note one next step.
Send one specific message today thanking someone for something they did that you never actually acknowledged at the time.
During one conversation today, watch the other person's face and posture for ten seconds before responding, and adjust your tone based on what you notice.
If you told someone something today that wasn't fully accurate, even a small exaggeration, go back and correct it before the day ends.
Choose one task you've been putting off and do the first ten minutes of it today, at a specific time you set now.
Think of someone who upset you recently and send them one small, low-stakes friendly message today, without mentioning what happened.
Before you finish work today, identify one task you're behind on and tell the person waiting on it, honestly and specifically, when they'll actually have it.
Say the one thing in a conversation today that you'd normally hold back because it might create friction, phrased calmly and respectfully.
Give away something specific today — your time, an hour of focused help, or an item you own — to someone who didn't ask for it.
Recall one specific person who helped you at a low point in the past and write them a short message naming exactly what they did.
The next time you're interrupted or delayed today, let it happen without sighing, checking your phone, or showing visible irritation, and notice how it feels.
Before making one decision today, write down what you'd tell a friend to do in your exact situation, and compare it honestly to what you're about to do.
Write one sentence naming why the work you're doing today actually matters to you, and reread it once before you start.
After one conversation today, privately write down one thing you did that you're not proud of in how you communicated, without excusing it.
